items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Mary Jane Patterson, Executive Director & Patrick Gilbride, Associate Director/Manager of Green Infrastructure Programs
notes:
Mary Jane Patterson and Patrick Gilbride from Reep Green Solutions appeared before the Committee to present the 2022-2023 Impact Report. P. Gilbride provided an overview of the number of meaningful actions, the 2020 inventory report, and home energy evaluations. P. Gilbride provided an overview of the climate adaption work, sharing that 330 homes have been supported in becoming more resilient to extreme heat and flooding. 

A copy of their presentation is attached to the minutes.

The Committee thanked M. Patterson for all work that they have done and welcomed P. Gilbride in their new role as Executive Director.

Responding to a question from the Committee, M. Patterson shared that they would love to see a program for low income energy efficiency.

items.title: Susan Weber, Woolwich
notes: Susan Weber appeared before the Committee to share their opposition to amalgamation and high density developments in Townships. S. Weber stated that policies should respect existing residential landscapes, as small towns have their own special character and should look and feel different than cities.

items.title: TSD-TRP-23-014, Update on Posted Speed Limits in School Zones (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Mike Henderson, Director, Transportation introduced the staff presentation, noting that these speed limit updates in school zones would help set consistent driver expectations moving forward.

Darryl Spencer, Manager, Transportation Engineering, provided a presentation which outlined the existing conditions within Regional school zones and observations from the pilot. D. Spencer noted that a benefit of adopting lower speed limits at all times, is that it would support schools and schoolyards to serve as community hubs.

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes.

Responding to questions from the Committee, D. Spencer shared that there will be a cost of approximately $20,000 to make changes to the signage, which will come out of a Council approved fund that transportation has for miscellaneous projects.

The Committee discussed and deliberated the report and the benefits of lowering speed limits all times versus only during school hours. Noted benefits of lowering the speed limit only during school hours, included more community buy-in and understanding. Concerns with lowering the speed limit at all times included the inability for automated speed enforcement (ASE) to have adjusted thresholds during different times of the day, and the lack of control over ticket pricing, as that is determined by the Province. Noted benefits for lowering the speed limits at all times included limiting confusion as to what the speed limit is, more consistency throughout the Region, and allowing schools to act as community hubs outside of school hours.

C. James assumed the Chair.

motions.item_title: TSD-TRP-23-013, Significant Weather Event - Delegated Authority for Declaration
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, amend the current Maintenance Agreement outlined in report,TES-TRP-21-19, Maintenance Agreement Report from October 2021, that authorized the current Maintenance Agreements with the three City Area Municipalities to; delegate authority to the Commissioner of Transportation Services or designate on behalf of the Region as set out in report TSD-TRP-23-013, dated November 7, 2023 to declare a Significant Weather Event (SWE) pursuant to Ontario Regulation O.Reg. 239/02 Minimum Maintenance Standards, (MMS) of the Municipal Act, 2001. And That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo amend By-law 16-023 to Regulate Traffic and Parking on Highways Under the Jurisdiction of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo to add the following, as Subsection 2(e) to; Part III – Enforcement and Authority: e) The Commissioner is authorized to declare a Significant Weather Event (SWE) in accordance with Ontario Regulation 239/02 Minimum Maintenance Standards for Municipal Highways. The Commissioner is authorized to further delegate that authority to declare a SWE to The Corporation of the City of Waterloo, The Corporation of the City of Kitchener, and The Corporation of the City of Cambridge in respect of a highway or part of a highway located within their respective municipal boundary.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, amend the current Maintenance Agreement outlined in report,TES-TRP-21-19, Maintenance Agreement Report from October 2021, that authorized the current Maintenance Agreements with the three City Area Municipalities to; delegate authority to the Commissioner of Transportation Services or designate on behalf of the Region as set out in report TSD-TRP-23-013, dated November 7, 2023 to declare a Significant Weather Event (SWE) pursuant to Ontario Regulation O.Reg. 239/02 Minimum Maintenance Standards, (MMS) of the Municipal Act, 2001. And

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo amend By-law 16-023 to Regulate Traffic and Parking on Highways Under the Jurisdiction of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo to add the following, as Subsection 2(e) to; Part III – Enforcement and Authority:

e) The Commissioner is authorized to declare a Significant Weather Event (SWE) in accordance with Ontario Regulation 239/02 Minimum Maintenance Standards for Municipal Highways. The Commissioner is authorized to further delegate that authority to declare a SWE to The Corporation of the City of Waterloo, The Corporation of the City of Kitchener, and The Corporation of the City of Cambridge in respect of a highway or part of a highway located within their respective municipal boundary.
